history.dynasty: Lavish renovation 1898-1910 by N. M. Subramanian Chettiar of Karaikudi and K.P.S. Palaniappa Chettiar of Kandanur; rajagopuram added 1968
history.period: Believed to be the earliest abode of Murugan (antiquity unverified); modern structure 1898-1968
history.summary: The Palani FOOTHILL temple, a separate shrine distinct from the Dhandayuthapani hill temple (seq 2277, id arulmigu-dhandayuthapani-swamy-temple-palani). The two form a composite unit: the foothill temple is the Kuzhandhai Velayuthaswami (child Murugan) shrine, about 200 m from the hill base beside the Saravana Poigai sacred tank, traditionally held to be Murugan's birthplace. Believed to have begun under the shade of a Nelli (amla) tree. Devotees usually visit this shrine before ascending the hill. Subsidiary shrines: Vinayagar, Annamalaiyar, Unnamulai Amman, Shani, Dhakshinamoorthy. Milk is offered as neivediyam after Balamurugan abhishekam; the temple is sought by couples desiring children. Shared opening hours with the hill temple and Periyanayaki Temple per temple festival invitations.

name: Thiruavinankudi Murugan Temple
town_description: The foothill shrine in Palani town (Dindigul district), on Sannathi Road / Giri Veethi near the Saravana Poigai tank, at the base of the Sivagiri hill.
tradition: Shaivite-affiliated Murugan worship (part of the Palani Murugan temple complex administration)
